text:
incident-bot: PAGER -> continuous-batching perf cliff detected on prod-cluster-a. KPIs: 95p latency spike, queue depth rising, KV cache evictions spiked. severity: P1. paging oncall: @eva.

incident-bot: Alert details: cluster=prod-cluster-a region=us-west-2 model=redwood-7b variant=quant2. recent change: autoscaler rolled a few pods ~10m ago. logs attached: /s3/infra/alerts/4299000001.log

eva: on it. pulling diagnostics now. seeing queue depth ~480 requests, avg microbatch size collapsed to 1 for many lanes. KV cache eviction rate 12k/s which looks like a runaway.

raj: I can jump in. are we seeing an input distribution change? any user spike?

oliver: support reports a customer (enterprise-acme) saw timeouts and partial generations ~10:08. they opened a ticket.

maria: telemetry: continuous-batch controller started to reduce batching window under high concurrency -> microbatch jitter increased. combined with prefetch ramp we appear to hit a resonance: frequent KV evictions causing longer cold loads which in turn stalls batching threads -> queueing.

eva: quick mitigation suggestion: 1) disable prefetch (controller flag) 2) lower max_concurrency_per_pod to drain surge 3) pin microbatch_min to 4 to avoid tiny microbatches. thoughts?

raj: agree. prioritizing actions: disable prefetch first (cheap, immediate). then set CONT_BATCH_MIN_MICROBATCH=4 via rollout.

sophia: can we quantify customer impact quickly? rough numbers?

maria: impact snapshot: 5% of requests elevated latency >3s, 0.9% error increase (transient 500s), affected hosts: 6/24 in cluster-a.

eva: applying prefetch disable now.

eva: ```
# disable prefetch on controller
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/cont-batch-controller PREFETCH_ENABLED=false --record
```

incident-bot: trigger: config-change detected by deploy-bot. rollout started.

raj: watching metrics. prefetch disable accepted, controllers rolled (3 pods). waiting for KV eviction rate to drop.

maria: KV eviction rate trending down 6k/s -> 2k/s after 40s. queue depth dropping from 480 -> 140. 95p latency improving.

oliver: support: customer-acme confirms partial generations receded, but still intermittent slowness.

eva: next step: pin microbatch min to avoid microbatch collapse. will patch the runtime config to set CONT_BATCH_MIN_MICROBATCH=4 and max_microbatch=8 on affected node pool.

eva: ```
# hotpatch runtime config
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.prod.redwood.ai/configs/cont-batch -d '{"CONT_BATCH_MIN_MICROBATCH":"4","CONT_BATCH_MAX_MICROBATCH":"8"}'
```

raj: rolling patch to nodepool canary 2 pods first. schedule at t+3m. keep prefetch off until stable.

maria: telemetry: after canary patch, microbatch distribution normalized (median 4, p90 6). queue depth stable ~50. KV evictions back to baseline.

eva: marking mitigation succeeded for now. keeping pager open for 30m to ensure stability.

sophia: product note: notify CS + affected customers that we've mitigated and are investigating root cause; likely combo of autoscaler + prefetch heuristic under sustained high-concurrency.

oliver: drafting customer message: "We observed intermittent timeouts due to internal batching and cache pressure. We've applied mitigations and are monitoring; will follow up with RCA."

raj: follow-up actions (short-term):
- revert autoscaler experiment on prod-cluster-a
- add a guardrail to prevent PREFETCH ramp on >60% concurrency
- add metric alert for KV eviction rate >5k/s for >1m

maria: follow-up (longer):
- rework prefetch heuristic to be workload-aware (respect microbatch distribution)
- add a smoothing window for microbatch sizing to reduce jitter
- fuzz-test controller under synthetic high-concurrency to reproduce resonance

eva: handing off to oncall rotation: @raj takes next 2h watch. I've put postmortem stub in /incidents/4299XXX-microbatch-resonance. please add logs and screenshots.

raj: taking it. will validate canary -> full rollout in 15m if stable.

incident-bot: note: page closed (acknowledged). escalation log created: INC-4299000001.

sophia: thanks team. please capture exact timings and the one-liner root-cause hypothesis for the RCA. :thumbsup:

oliver: added customer ticket link: #ACME-5123 to the incident doc.

maria: leaving small TODO: correlate autoscaler events around 10:00-10:10 with prefetch policy changes.

eva: closing thread once postmortem is ready. short summary for ops: PREFETCH_DISABLED, MIN_MICROBATCH=4, monitor eviction-rate alert.

raj: ack.
